description: Generic Stage Route Model hardware profile. Every kernel is derived from transformed TTIR resource workloads; absolute time adds measured kernel-boundary and global-load completion envelopes selected only by structural route facts. No operator identity, exact function DAG signature, shape whitelist, or kernel-specific elapsed intercept participates in scoring or prediction.

selection_calibration.description: The only structural threshold consumed by the Stage partitioner. Numerical Stage costs come from mode-specific resource formulas and referenced measurements; obsolete route penalties and multipliers have been removed.
selection_calibration.source: StagePartitioner uses this architecture-independent boundary to select the tiny-dot formula family. It is a semantic model-domain limit, not a fitted route multiplier.

simd.description: Inputs used to estimate the all-SIMD candidate: SIMD width, setup, operation, memory, and dot costs.

startup_system_cycles.description: One-time SIMD Stage startup proxy measured with a compile-time-specialized minimal observable vector body and matching barrier-only subtraction.
startup_system_cycles.note: The consumed vector value is measured; memory-transfer startup is modeled per logical memory operation.

f32.add.description: Measured FP32 SIMD add base throughput resolved from the shared microbenchmark profile.

fp32.saturated.description: Execution lower bound for every numeric TTIR operation without a dedicated operation profile. Each semantic operation retains its TTIR name in the workload and pays at least one 2048-bit SIMD work unit at the measured saturated FP32 arithmetic rate; shape, address, view, and layout-only operations are excluded.

f32.max.description: Measured FP32 SIMD maximum throughput plus the semantic maximum lowering completion paid once per dynamic tensor operation; evidence: data_provider/950pr_simd_semantic_maximum_completion_20261011.json.

f32.relu.description: The __hmf_reluf helper uses the measured maximum-class vector throughput but does not lower through the binary semantic-maximum completion path. Fresh A5 ReLU holdout timing remains the independent validation point.

f32.exp.description: Measured effective FP32 SIMD exponential throughput.

f32.log.description: Measured effective FP32 SIMD logarithm throughput.

f32.sqrt.description: FP32 SIMD square-root lowers to one vector arithmetic operation in the audited pytest and operation-chain controls; use the measured vector arithmetic issue curve.

f32.cos.description: Effective SIMD cosine completion from the fresh 1024-element dependent operation-chain slope. The factor represents the complete backend cosine expansion per semantic vector operation.

predicate.cmp.description: Measured standalone semantic SIMD comparison throughput.

convert.cast.description: Measured effective SIMD cast throughput per semantic cast.

f32.clamp.description: Measured effective SIMD throughput per semantic clamp.

layout.transpose.description: SIMD transpose exchange throughput. Work is logical elements times the moved innermost-axis extent.

histogram.i32.description: Completion rate of the SIMD i32 histogram helper. Work units are 2048-bit SIMD vector instructions derived from the TTIR source tensor element count; bin width remains visible in the explicit result store. The fit uses fresh forced-SIMD A5 M=256/512/1024/2048, BINS=2 controls plus BINS=4/8 holdouts.

memory.description: Model-specific all-SIMD memory rates consumed by StageCostModel.

independent_loop_load_group.description: Generic MTE2 envelope for one to four uninterrupted contiguous FP32 load streams in one independent loop. One full-grid kernel startup is followed by one shared iteration startup plus aggregate bytes divided by the fitted group rate.
independent_loop_load_group.evidence: bench_simd_memory_groups.py: original six 2/3/4-stream points plus fresh flat rank-one one-load controls at 19 and 37 loop iterations (4.730 and 7.629 us). The single-load loop has the same serialized load/store service domain; sub-grid launches transfer the full-grid startup to kernel-boundary ownership. Rank-two masked tiles keep the analytical per-row transfer path because they are outside the one-stream evidence geometry.

computed_address_scalarized_load.evidence: Fresh A5 forced-SIMD non-affine computed-address sweep recorded in microbench/data_provider/950pr_simd_computed_address_scalarization_20261009.json. NPUIR lowers each logical lane to scalar float address computation followed by scalar GM load. BLOCK 16 and 64 determine the bounded per-lane completion rate; BLOCK 8 and 32 are fit holdouts, and BLOCK 24 and 48 are untouched holdouts. Selection uses only the TTIR address DAG, unknown rank-one layout, element count and absence of loaded-index dependence.

control_flow_address_scalarized_load.evidence: Fresh A5 forced-SIMD scalar-control-flow tensor-address sweep in v117_conditional_address_scalarization_sweep_20261009. NPUIR lowers the rank-one FP32 load to a scalar scf.for over lanes after the TTIR address is selected by scf.if. Extents 8, 16, 32 and 64 define the bounded residual curve; extents 24 and 48 are untouched interpolation holdouts. Selection uses only address provenance, dtype, layout and tensor extent.

masked_load_store_read_modify_write.evidence: Fresh A5 forced-SIMD rank-two FP16 masked load/add/store sweep recorded in microbench/data_provider/950pr_simd_masked_store_read_modify_write_20261009.json. NPUIR consistently adds a destination GM load before the masked merge and store. Curves are bounded by physical row width and statically proven active rows; row-bytes=16 active-rows=6 plus row-bytes=32 active-rows=9 and row-bytes=64 active-rows=18 are interpolation holdouts. Admission additionally requires an exact shared mask and a TTIR store-value dependency on the matching load.

irregular_tile_completion.evidence: Generic rectangular controls on healthy A5 cards. Physical/active coefficients use development geometries 32x256/150, 80x256/150, and 48x256 with active widths 64 and 200; production 64x256/150 is held out. The row72/row80 boundary sweep and fresh-process row80 copy/softmax controls measure a 0.70 masked completion efficiency above the <=72 small-row lowering regime; reduction is an independent non-masked-floor-dominated control. Independent width-150 rows32/64 determine the 0.065 tail rate. Aligned width-128 rows32/64 determine a 32-row completion curve: 0.065 cycles/element for the first full group and 0.044 for each additional group; width-64 rows16 remains an independent narrow control. Fresh forced-SIMD rows48/64/72 and row64 Q=4/8/12/16/22 controls in data_provider/950pr_simd_structural_completion_20261008.json separate resident row-group ownership from complete-kernel footprint. The two-complete-row-group geometry retains 0.425 of physical materialization below the boundary. Q4 and Q16 are development points; Q8 and Q12 are interpolation holdouts. At Q22 the aggregate TTIR read/write footprint exceeds the 128 MiB hardware boundary and the full physical materialization is restored; rows48-Q12 and rows72-Q12 remain independent geometry/footprint holdouts below it. All Stage iterations remain serialized. The rules use TTIR geometry, byte workload, trip count, and launch grid only, with no operator or exact-shape key.

8.evidence: bench_simd_strided_store.py fit on rows 16/32/64 plus held-out masked-layout reductions at rows 80. The existing linear extra-lane extrapolation predicts both row-80 cases within 4%; domain is limited to 96 rows.

16.evidence: bench_simd_strided_store.py, five 16-byte-row-stride points over rows 16/32/64 and 1/2/4 stores; in-sample max error 5.80%, medium-confidence interpolation domain.

32.evidence: bench_simd_strided_store.py, five 32-byte-row-stride points over rows 32/64 and 1/2/4 stores; in-sample max error 5.43%, medium-confidence interpolation domain.

64.evidence: Fresh A5 compiler-equivalent forced-SIMD masked compaction controls at 128 and 256 rows per source iteration, eight static iterations, and a 64-byte FP32 row stride. Matching requires one masked rank-one strided load, one masked rank-one contiguous store, equal semantic element counts, no loaded-index address, no control/synchronization, and distinct load/store mask provenance.

Fresh A5 compiler-equivalent forced-SIMD masked scatter controls at 128 and 256 rows per source iteration, eight static iterations, and a 64-byte FP32 row stride. The separate destination predicate exposes the backend strided-store completion path; a shared-predicate load/store control is excluded structurally.

memory.note: Uncovered operations retain startup-per-operation plus byte throughput. Proven uninterrupted independent-loop groups use the generic grouped envelopes above.

strided_short_completion.description: Closed-form strided load/store completion fits for the SIMD StridedShort direct-access domain. Each slot fixes a formula shape in StageCostModels.cpp and supplies only its fitted numbers. Calibrated from rotate-loop Event slopes (2000/8000 iterations), so a slot is a steady-state marginal per-iteration cost and requires an owning loop. Compile-time-constant stride, affine address, static shape and non-indirect provenance only. Load and SIMT slots price masked and unmasked alike (a runtime all-true mask measured free); the two simd_store_masked_* slots are the masked-only exception, because a mask forces the destination to be read back before the write.

simd_load_stride2_r2.evidence: PHYS3_simd_load_stride2_r2.json; 120 points, branch A src>=32 (n=87, MAPE 2.95%) / branch B src<32 (n=33, MAPE 8.52%)

simd_load_stride_gt2_r1_dense.evidence: PHYS3_simd_load_stride_gt2_r1_dense.json; 136 points, n>=32 and ISB<=128, MAPE 8.70%. Dense regime ISB<=32 only; see simd_load_stride_gt2_r1_sparse.

simd_load_stride_gt2_r1_sparse.evidence: ISB>32 B sparse segment, 45 points, four terms (intercept, n, n*eb, mx64), weighted least squares w=1/T, MAPE 8.88%. Rescanned 2026-10-18 with the probe AUTO rotate window (per-point step = tile span, 33-67 MB); the historical fixed step 8192 x mask 16383 streamed 262 MB per launch and inflated this regime up to 2.2x. K-marginal on the pytest_strided_compaction geometry (n=256, ISB=64 B, eb=4): 231.70 ns vs 221.78 measured, +4.5%.

simd_store_masked_stride_gt2.evidence: data_provider/strided_ldst/pre-explore/results/final/errors_masked_store.csv, stride>=3 branch; 384 points (int8/float16/float32, n=4..512, stride=3/4/5/6/8/16/32/64/128, 15 rank-two shapes), MAPE 6.96%. Masked-only: a runtime mask makes the SIMD store read the destination back, so the fit carries an extra 1 KB aggregate term. Worst regime is stride>=32 with n<=16 (40-56%, 15/384 points), see README 3.5(a).

simd_store_masked_stride2.evidence: data_provider/strided_ldst/pre-explore/results/final/errors_masked_store.csv, stride==2 branch; 100 points, MAPE 7.08%. Same shape as simd_store_masked_stride_gt2 with its own numbers: stride 2 lowers through DeinterleaveStatusOptimization (block move plus extract_slice), so the fixed and read-modify-write terms are visibly cheaper. Masked-only.

reduction.description: Generic FP32 SIMD row-reduction envelope: one startup per semantic tt.reduce plus aggregate reduction lane-steps divided by the measured rate.

scalarized_multi_result.evidence: Fresh A5 v112 argmax-like paired-value/index tt.reduce surface. Extents 32, 64 and 125 fit the scalarized nested-loop lowering; 48x128 is an untouched holdout at +0.35%. Extent 16 follows a different route and is excluded. Selection uses only TTIR row count, reduction extent, result count and element width.

reduction.source: bench_simd_reduction_rate.py paired contiguous-output reduction/control sweep; five independent shape/repeat points, with each point held out in turn. One-trip zero-filled masked accumulators additionally use the exact runtime active prefix and a separately measured one-time completion setup from data_provider/950pr_simd_structural_completion_20261008.json.

sort.description: Bounded SIMD native-vsort completion surface. Within the calibrated FP32 axis range, service scales with independent rows and is nearly invariant to the row extent.
sort.evidence: Fresh A5 v112 ascend.sort to hivm.hir.vsort sweep. 64x16 and 128x16 are fit points; 256x16 is an untouched holdout at +0.31%, while extent-8 and extent-32 controls remain within 1.5%. Selection uses only TTIR rows, axis extent and element width.

dot.description: SIMD tiny-dot cost: dynamic matrix instances times setup plus aggregate FLOPs divided by dependent-chain throughput.
dot.source: Ascend950PR dependent N=16/N=32 dot-chain joint fit with one final store

stage_resources.description: Generic SIMD front-end inputs. Unclassified scalar and control instructions contribute only to the measured shared issue lower bound. Non-uniform loaded-index tensors use isolated transaction-count curves because SIMD lowering scalarizes lane addresses. Loaded-index atomic service uses the common multi-program rate plus a separate measured one-physical-program rate; contiguous atomic addresses retain the default vector rate. A 128/512/2048-element used-versus-unused FP32 atomic surface separates result dependency from atomic service and final-store work.

prefix_scan.description: Additive SIMD scans retain the measured dependent-vector-add formula. Non-additive straight-line helpers use completion curves selected by the returned TTIR combine class and semantic scan geometry.

minmax.evidence: Fresh forced-SIMD A5 cummax structural surface at rows/extent 8x32, 16x32, 32x32, 16x64 and 8x128. The joint fit prices semantic elements and the serial scan-axis dependency separately after subtracting the generic kernel boundary and explicit non-scan Stages; no operator name or exact shape participates online. A one-sequence backend-helper path is selected by independent_sequence_count=1 and uses the extent curve in data_provider/950pr_simd_structural_completion_20261008.json; multi-sequence geometry retains the aggregate-work/dependency formula.

non_unit_axis_stride_completion.evidence: Fresh forced-SIMD A5 strided cummin TTIR surface at X=1/2/3/4, axis extent=3/5/8 and physical axis stride=4/7/8. The bounded linear completion fit uses only semantic elements after subtracting the generic kernel boundary and explicit load/store stages; the online match is combine class, stride, extent, result arity and work range.

mul.evidence: Fresh forced-SIMD A5 cumprod structural surface at rows/extent 8x32, 16x32, 32x32, 16x64 and 8x128. The joint fit prices semantic elements and the serial scan-axis dependency separately after subtracting the generic kernel boundary and explicit non-scan Stages; no operator name or exact shape participates online. A one-sequence backend-helper path is selected by independent_sequence_count=1 and uses the extent curve in data_provider/950pr_simd_structural_completion_20261008.json; multi-sequence geometry retains the aggregate-work/dependency formula.

prefix_scan.reverse_extent_legality_evidence: Fresh A5 W512 reverse SIMD cumsum failed at device synchronize with 507035; the same W512 reverse kernel succeeds in SIMT. W128/W256 reverse SIMD execute correctly. This is a target/compiler route-legality bound, not a cost fit.

loop_carried_recurrence.description: Measured lower bound for one physical group's iteration of a reduction recurrence. The work-size key is reduction lane-steps per logical program; SIMD has only factor 1.

single_result_row_reduction_completion.evidence: data_provider/950pr_simd_single_result_row_reduction_recurrence_20261009.json; endpoint fit uses P=8/32 and T=4/16 only. P=16,T=8 and reduction extents 64/256 are untouched structural holdouts, all within 3.5%. The matcher uses recurrence/reduction geometry and bounded source program count; no operator or kernel name is consumed.

continuous_memory.description: Measured physical-group execution envelope for ordinary contiguous FP32 transfers. Curves are consumed only inside the measured byte interval; operation count is multiplied once and route composition multiplies runtime waves once.

mixed_parent_memory_completion.evidence: A5 card4 cv_transition_solve_tail_full/transition v75: independent 10-load/10-store FP32 16x16 parent-memory probes at P=224,1024,1536,2048,3072,4096 and row strides 64/8192/16384 bytes. Q<=55 is the holdout-safe base domain; the large-Q slope is cross-checked by six solve_tril shapes and is applied from compiler-derived parent bytes/Q only.

stage_resources.source: Ascend950PR versioned microbenchmark evidence. The loaded-index slope is measured independently by probe_indirect_gather_rate.py. data_provider/950pr_simd_indirect_startup_ownership_20261006.json shows why the raw one-wave count-fit intercept is not added: it already contains the separately modeled 56-program kernel boundary and final-store/control stages. Its transaction-count parameter is shared by scalarized FP16/FP32 SIMD accesses; uncovered transfers retain explicit analytical fallback.

grid_stride_loop.description: Dynamic source-loop SIMD dot and prefix-scan curves from isolated Q sweeps. Curves are selected from compiler-derived loop structure and workload geometry; no cross-stage pipeline overlap is assumed. The matching dynamic loaded-index curve is stored under indirect_memory.grid_stride_load_* so the common parser applies it only to compiler-proven grid-stride stages.

two_pass_rowwise_completion.evidence: data_provider/950pr_two_pass_rowwise_completion_20261007.json; forced-SIMD development points use extents 256/512/1024 and Q=2/3/5/8. Untouched extent-768,Q=3 and extent-1024,Q=4 interpolation holdouts are within 3.2%. Matching is the compiler-derived two-segment/two-read/one-reduction/no-dot structure; no kernel or operator identity is consumed and execution remains serialized.

scalar_memory.description: SIMD scalar white-box: MainScalar load T=prep+fill+max(0,K-outstanding)*extra_line+(K-1)*issue; scalar store lowers to MTE3 T=prep+fill. Values are CAModel core cycles converted by 988.9/1800.
scalar_memory.evidence: Upstream 7e1107f89 target white-box coefficients from CAModel; resource-level target constants, independent of kernel identity.

simt.description: Inputs used to estimate the all-SIMT candidate and the SIMT portion of a mixed candidate.

setup_system_cycles.description: Completion-inclusive minimal-SIMT-VF net setup selected by launched warp count. All entries use compile-time-specialized binaries and subtract the matching barrier-only loop.

f32.add.description: Measured FP32 SIMT scalar-add base throughput resolved from the shared microbenchmark profile.

fp32.saturated.description: Execution lower bound for every numeric TTIR operation without a dedicated operation profile. Each semantic operation retains its TTIR name in the workload and pays at least one lane operation at the measured active-warp FP32 arithmetic saturation rate; shape, address, view, and layout-only operations are excluded.

f32.relu.description: SIMT ReLU helper inherits maximum-class scalar throughput while retaining its distinct semantic operation class.

f32.exp.description: Measured effective FP32 SIMT exponential throughput.

f32.log.description: Measured effective FP32 SIMT logarithm throughput.

f32.sqrt.description: FP32 SIMT square-root lowers to one scalar arithmetic instruction in the audited operation-chain controls; inherit the active-warp arithmetic throughput curve.

f32.cos.description: Effective SIMT cosine completion from the fresh 1024-element dependent operation-chain slope. The factor applies to every active-warp point of the measured scalar arithmetic curve.

predicate.cmp.description: Measured standalone semantic SIMT comparison throughput.

convert.cast.description: Measured effective SIMT cast throughput per semantic cast.

f32.clamp.description: Measured effective SIMT throughput per semantic clamp.

layout.transpose.description: Conservative SIMT fallback for transpose exchange workload.

histogram.i32.description: Completion-inclusive local-SIMT i32 histogram curve refreshed with the clean TA c3f4182c20a0 and NPUIR 03c14949b065 toolchain. Repository-native 8192-row sweeps cover 64/128/256 bins and uniform/single-bin/radix inputs; the 133.173278-cycle startup is the median structural residual across those nine points. The knee at 128 work units is the four-warp lane capacity, and the fixed local-scope envelope is already present in the observed semantic completion.

dot.description: SIMT tiny-dot cost: dynamic matrix instances times measured setup plus aggregate FLOPs divided by measured dependent-chain throughput.
dot.source: Ascend950PR accumulator-feedback dependent-dot chain sweeps. The 4-warp base comes from the N=16/N=32 joint fit; the 8/16 active-warp rates use the conservative lower aggregate gain from independent size-16, size-32 and size-64 count-8/count-16 F sweeps. The occupancy curve is consumed only by loop-carried dot recurrence Stages; straight-line tiny-cube Stages retain the base rate.

shuffle.description: SIMT workload-effective shuffle rate resolved from the shared runtime-loop microbenchmark. Route-level generalization confidence is intentionally lower than measurement repeatability.

memory.description: SIMT workload-effective GM load/store rates resolved from sequential rotating runtime-loop measurements. Indirect/random/coalescing behavior is not calibrated by these rates.

64.evidence: Fresh A5 compiler-equivalent whole-SIMT masked compaction controls at 128 and 256 rows per source iteration, eight static iterations, and a 64-byte FP32 row stride. The curve is a bounded strided-load resource floor and keeps contiguous store, predicate and issue work explicit.

data_provider/950pr_simt_masked_strided_store_completion_debug0_20261011.json; fresh A5 production-mode (TRITON_DEBUG=0) whole-SIMT and Auto-selected whole-SIMT masked scatter controls at 128 and 256 rows per source iteration, eight static iterations, and a 64-byte FP32 row stride. The curve is a bounded strided-store resource floor selected from TTIR access direction and mask provenance.

strided_short_completion.description: Closed-form strided load/store completion fits for the SIMT StridedShort direct-access domain. Each slot fixes a formula shape in StageCostModels.cpp and supplies only its fitted numbers. Calibrated from rotate-loop Event slopes (2000/8000 iterations), so a slot is a steady-state marginal per-iteration cost and requires an owning loop. Unmasked, compile-time-constant stride, affine address, static shape and non-indirect provenance only.

stage_resources.description: Generic SIMT front-end inputs. Unclassified scalar and control instructions contribute only to the measured shared issue lower bound. Prefix-scan issue accounting preserves operation boundaries. The loaded-index atomic rate is the common P1/P56 residual slope from fresh race-free i32 permutation probes; ordinary atomic addresses retain the default warp-parallel rate.

prefix_scan.description: Grid-stride and recurrence scans use the decomposed dependency model. A P=1 straight-line scan lowers to a completion-inclusive external helper priced from TTIR semantic elements.
prefix_scan.straight_line_completion_evidence: Fresh A5 profiler controls for non-additive and multiplicative straight-line scans: cummax rows/extent 8x64, 16x32, 32x16 and cumprod 1x1024, 2x512, 4x256. After subtracting the generic kernel boundary and explicit GM load/store Stages, semantic_elements/10 SYS_CNT plus helper ownership of the pure generic index prologue keeps all six geometries within ten percent without an operator or exact-shape key.

rowwise_reduction.description: Completion-inclusive physical-group surface for a structural TTIR FP32 row reduction with one packed rank-2 input and two reduction operations. Online interpolation is bounded to the measured row/extent rectangle and never uses an operator or kernel name.
rowwise_reduction.evidence: data_provider/950pr_simt_rowwise_reduction_structural_surface_20261006.json; independent 3x3 TTIR row/extent grid for F1/F2/F4, k=9 iteration-linearity holdout max 1.86%; runtime-wave holdouts kept outside the fit

multi_result_reduction.description: Whole-SIMT F1 completion body for one FP32 two-result tt.reduce whose reduction axis pads to 128. The backend template is selected by the exact non-power-of-two tail class; each bounded row curve uses the next measured row-group bucket because a partial backend group executes the full template.
multi_result_reduction.evidence: Fresh A5 v113 structural sweeps under the Auto whole-SIMT route. Development curves use extent 124 (divisible-by-4 tail), 126 (mod-4-equals-2 tail), and 125 (odd tail) across rows 8..64. Independent extents 80/96/112/120, 121/122/123/127, cross-card repeats, and an argmin comparator holdout confirm that padded extent, tail class and row geometry select the lowering; no operator or exact source shape is consumed. Disassembly shows the odd-tail SHFL stream doubles from 486 to 972 when padded rows cross 32, explaining the observed completion cliff. Power-of-two axes retain the analytical reduction path.

two_pass_rowwise_completion.evidence: data_provider/950pr_two_pass_rowwise_completion_20261007.json; explicit F2/F4 structural controls cover Q=2..8 and extents 256/512/768/1024. F4 Q=6/7 were untouched interpolation holdouts and are within 1.1%. The signed residual corrects serialized route composition after independent Stage resource accounting; no pipeline overlap, kernel name or operator name is used.

loop_carried_recurrence.description: Measured lower bound for one physical SuperBlock group's iteration of a reduction recurrence. Each inner work-size key is reduction lane-steps in one logical program; the measured value already includes all F logical programs in the physical group.

single_result_row_reduction_completion.evidence: data_provider/950pr_simt_single_result_row_reduction_recurrence_20261009.json; the structural fit uses P16/T4, P16/T16 and P32/T16 endpoints for one FP32 extent-128 reduction per dynamic recurrence iteration. P16/T8 and independent P24/T8/T12 cases are interpolation holdouts. Matching uses only TTIR recurrence/reduction geometry, trip count, factor and source launch count.

continuous_memory.description: Measured physical-group execution envelope for ordinary contiguous FP32 transfers. Each factor-specific value already includes all logical programs grouped by that SuperBlock factor; the Stage formula must not multiply it by F again.

layout_memory.description: Measured factor-specific strided-wide FP32 memory layout curves. Keys encode complete access geometry, dtype, masking, active warps and SuperBlock factor, so the evidence can be consumed by any matching Stage.

scope_handoff.description: One Stage materializes as one compound scope.scope; Mixed is illegal for a single Stage. C_scope = C_body(cv efficiency) + C_boundary_data + C_fixed_scope + [CV1:N]*C_cross_core_sync. C_fixed_scope=277 SYS_CNT is the median one-scope delta from exact-lowering AIV-only probes at independent tensor widths 16/64/256 (0.353/0.167/0.277 us). The CV fields are explicit uncalibrated fallbacks and remain neutral until the independent paired pure/mixed structural sweep is complete; they must not be fitted from an operator or exact shape.

stage_resources.source: Ascend950PR versioned microbenchmark evidence. The issue floor is an observable conservative bound, not a claimed microarchitecture peak. Control instructions enter that shared floor but do not receive fabricated additive latency. Loaded-index loads use the measured operation-shape curve; scope hand-off retains explicitly marked fallback parameters.

store_footprint_service.evidence: 950pr_simt_layout_service_20260918.json reproduces the fit: 950PR device4, full sweep ew6SfU, 36 held-out layout/warp points, max slope error 5.216%. SYS_CNT, 64-bit/lane, hot GM. Online use restricted to nonpacked nonoverlapping rows: packed issue-floor transfer failed in grouped repeat Xw1NYC. Service estimate only, not first-round, barrier, private/shared, layout-conversion or complete Stage calibration.

grid_stride_loop.indirect_dot_composition_evidence: The F4 signed adjustment is fitted only from isolated source-grid-stride gather-dot structural probes at development Q=1,3,5,8. Untouched Q=2,4 F4 validation has 0.52% maximum error. F1/F2 retain the existing generic formula because the full Level1 generalization harness already keeps those factors within 10%, while the lower profiler protocol used by the structural sweep does not transfer its signed startup adjustment to the Level1 low-Q timing target. Geometry comes from compiler-derived in-loop loaded-index warp instructions and dot FLOPs; the surface is bounded, contains no kernel/operator key, and assumes serialized execution without pipeline overlap.
grid_stride_loop.description: Dynamic source loops serialize successive bodies on one resident program. These isolated curves are distinct from static-range unrolled curves and do not model pipeline overlap.

resident_direct_memory.evidence: Fresh explicit-SIMT factor1 sweep on healthy A5 card3 at total direct FP32 footprints 3, 6, 12, 24, 48 and 96 MiB. The 3-48 MiB points form one steady resident regime; 96 MiB is held out on the existing rotating/cold rates. Independent 2-load/1-store and 4-load/1-store bodies identify load/store rates without an operator name, kernel name, or exact-shape condition. Source grid-stride F1/F2/F4 controls execute the same serialized source body and therefore share this resource curve; no pipeline overlap is modeled.

scalar_memory.description: SIMT warp-uniform scalar white-box: diff-line load T=prep+fill+(K-1)*issue; first scalar store T=base. Values are CAModel core cycles converted by 988.9/1800.
scalar_memory.evidence: Upstream 7e1107f89 target white-box coefficients from CAModel; resource-level target constants, independent of kernel identity.

kernel_timing.description: Kernel-boundary residual after subtracting the minimal store-only kernel's modeled Stage work. A separate route-keyed residual is composed once when transformed TTIR contains a global load. A measured structural curve also completes the SIMD nested-scalar lowering of tiny rank-2 loaded-index tiles and participates in route ranking. Prologue/epilogue values are only an accounting split.

kernel_timing.evidence: The base curve is the fresh forced-SIMD minimal observable store-only kernel sweep at physical grids 1,2,4,8,16,32,56. The global-load residual is the median direct-copy profiler duration minus its compiler-derived route resource and the base boundary at P=1: 314.207 SYS_CNT for forced SIMD and 485.789 SYS_CNT for selected SIMT. Independent P=4/P=56 direct-copy controls confirm the term is a sub-microsecond completion envelope rather than a per-operation slope. Kernel argument count is reported for diagnosis only: the v105 held-out set disproved an additive argument-count charge because two four-argument kernels with different structural work required opposite corrections. The prologue/epilogue fields are an equal accounting split, not separately measured components.
